documents.title: UA Ethical Use of AI Statement
documents.stance_why: The statement sets no rule of its own: it says "Students should look to their instructors for guidance on the fair and ethical use of AI tools for this course" and only warns that inappropriate use is misconduct, so the decision is delegated to instructors.
documents.summary: A short university Ethical Use of AI statement quoted on a library guide. It calls AI useful for learning, tells students to follow instructor guidance, and says inappropriate use violates the Code of Student Conduct.

units.why: The statement calls AI "powerful tools that can be used to aid in the learning process", a benefit claim that frames the rest without setting a rule; so it is informs and P87 (benefits of AI), not a permission.
units.anchor: powerful tools that can be used to aid in the learning process

units.why: "Students should look to their instructors for guidance" hands the decision on AI use to the course instructor and sets no university rule, so it is P04 and a should for students at course level.
units.anchor: Students should look to their instructors for guidance
units.frag_start: Students should look to their instructors
units.frag_end: use of AI tools for this course.

units.why: "The inappropriate or unethical use of such technologies will violate the Code of Student Conduct as cheating, plagiarism, fabrication..." classifies misuse as misconduct handled by an existing process, which is P36.
units.anchor: will violate the Code of Student Conduct as cheating, plagiarism, fabrication

units.why: The passage says misconduct is "reported to the Department of Student Conduct and Community Standards", naming the office that runs the process; this is P80 (who enforces) rather than P81 because it describes the office, not steps instructors must follow.
units.anchor: reported to the Department of Student Conduct and Community Standards
units.frag_start: The Code of Student Conduct is
units.policy: The Code of Student Conduct is a University rule that provides the framework for the student conduct process and defines student misconduct; misconduct is reported to the Department of Student Conduct and Community Standards.
units.fit_note: Describes the office handling misconduct generally, not an AI-specific owner of the AI policy.

units.why: "Students ... are responsible to know and abide by the Code of Student Conduct and all University rules, regulations, and policies" binds students to existing university rules, which is P77; it is not P78 because it names the Code, not course AI rules.
units.anchor: responsible to know and abide by the Code of Student Conduct
